skill.name: apktool
skill.description: Guides authorized Android APK reverse engineering with apktool, including unpacking, manifest inspection, resource searches, smali review, rebuilding, signing, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Guide authorized APK reverse engineering and security inspection with apktool.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples, literal search terms, and signing examples in SKILL.md. The skill is legitimate apktool guidance for authorized APK analysis, but it includes dual-use credential discovery language that should be tightened before publication.

remediation.issue: Credential discovery workflow can be misused against IoT devices.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization before credential searches and remove or narrow guidance about testing extracted credentials against devices.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be copied with untrusted file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to quote paths, avoid shell interpolation, and run commands only in a controlled working directory.

remediation.issue: Repackaging guidance can produce distributable modified APKs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing ethics warning and add a reminder before rebuild and signing steps that redistribution requires permission.

semantic_findings.title: Dual-Use Credential Discovery and Testing Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill pairs APK credential discovery with guidance to test credentials against IoT devices. This can support authorized research, but it can also enable misuse without stronger authorization gates.

content.value_statement: Android APK analysis can require many repeated apktool, manifest, and resource inspection steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe unpacking, inspection, and repackaging workflows.
actual_capabilities: Decode APK files with apktool and organize output directories.
Inspect AndroidManifest.xml for permissions, exported components, debug flags, and network security settings.
Search resources and smali files for URLs, credentials, cryptography, and file operations.
Inspect native libraries with file and strings commands.
Rebuild, sign, verify, and align modified APKs when authorized.
Troubleshoot framework, resource, path, memory, build, and signing errors.
limitations: Requires apktool, Java, and related Android build tools to be installed.
Does not decompile smali into readable Java; it suggests jadx for that task.
Cannot determine whether an APK may be legally analyzed; users must confirm authorization.
May need vendor framework files for system or manufacturer APKs.

use_cases.title: Review a Client APK
use_cases.description: Decode an authorized Android app and inspect its manifest, resources, exported components, and hardcoded configuration.

use_cases.title: Inspect Release Artifacts
use_cases.description: Verify that a build is not debuggable, exposes no unexpected components, and can be rebuilt only when needed.

use_cases.title: Map IoT App Communication
use_cases.description: Extract endpoints, device strings, and certificate pinning clues from an authorized companion app assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Decode an APK
prompt_templates.prompt: I have permission to analyze app.apk. Use apktool to decode it into app-unpacked and summarize the output structure.

prompt_templates.title: Review Manifest Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this decoded APK directory. Review AndroidManifest.xml for permissions, exported components, debug flags, backup settings, and network security configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Search Resources and Smali
prompt_templates.prompt: For this authorized APK, search resources and smali for URLs, hardcoded secrets, cryptography usage, and native library loading. Prioritize findings by risk.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild and Troubleshoot
prompt_templates.prompt: I modified an authorized decoded APK. Rebuild, sign, verify, and troubleshoot install failures while preserving notes about each step.

output_examples.output: A concise findings report listing permissions, exported components, hardcoded endpoints, resource locations, and recommended follow-up checks.
A short diagnosis with the likely missing framework file, the corrective apktool step, and when to retry decoding.

output_examples.input: Summarize an IoT companion app assessment.
output_examples.output: An endpoint inventory, device communication notes, certificate pinning clues, and evidence paths inside the decoded APK.

best_practices: Confirm authorization before decoding, modifying, or testing any APK.
Work on copies and keep original APK files unchanged.
Document package version, permissions, exported components, endpoints, and evidence locations.
anti_patterns: Do not run analysis on APKs you do not own or have permission to assess.
Do not distribute rebuilt APKs without explicit authorization.
Do not treat search results as proof before manually verifying context.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides apktool workflows for unpacking, inspecting, rebuilding, signing, and troubleshooting Android APK files.

faq.question: Does it require apktool to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The local environment needs apktool and a Java runtime before the commands can work.

faq.question: Can it decompile APKs into Java source?
faq.answer: No. Apktool produces resources and smali. The skill recommends jadx when readable Java output is needed.

faq.question: Can it modify and rebuild APKs?
faq.answer: Yes, when authorized. It includes build, signing, verification, and zipalign guidance for modified APKs.

faq.question: Is this only for security teams?
faq.answer: No. Developers can use it to inspect release artifacts, resources, manifests, and packaging issues.

faq.question: What authorization is needed?
faq.answer: Only analyze APKs you own or have explicit permission to assess. Follow licensing, terms, and disclosure rules.
